Subject: Request: CAIQ control mapping and evidence for OmniTrade evaluation

Hi Logan / Laura,

Thanks for taking this on. OmniTrade is running a 3rd-party security review ahead of our procurement committee next month and we need a CAIQ-style control crosswalk plus sample evidence for a subset of controls. Primary asks:

- A CAIQ control matrix (mapping Redwood controls to CSA questions) scoped to PII processing, network segregation, KMS/keys, and logging/retention.
- Representative evidence for: key rotation policy & logs, network configuration diagram showing VPC boundaries, and sample audit/log extracts for 30 days.
- A short owner table showing who at Redwood owns each control and the recommended artefact filename.

Can you confirm feasibility and whether you can deliver an initial package by EOD Thursday, Jan 15 (3 business days)? Also, any controls you cannot substantiate, please flag so we can route follow-ups to our procurement team.

If helpful, Jonah from BlueHarbor (cc) is our external auditor and can accept SFTP or shared-drive bundles.

Best,
Jessica Marlowe
Security Evaluation Lead
OmniTrade Inc
security@omnitrade.com

   - Evidence manifest (text file) with descriptions and retention windows.
   - Sample artifacts: KMS rotation logs, infra diagram, and 30-day log extract (redacted).

2) Owner contacts: Laura will own infra/network artifacts; Rishi will own KMS and key rotation logs; Kimberly will curate logging/retention extracts.

3) Transfer mechanism: we can deliver via a secured shared Drive link or SFTP. Please advise preference — we default to a restricted Drive folder.

4) Exceptions: any control where we rely on partner-managed infra (if applicable) will be annotated in the crosswalk and flagged for follow-up.

I'll attach the initial crosswalk draft and a manifest in a separate message once Laura/Rishi have pulled the artifacts. If you're open, let's do a 30-minute sync tomorrow to walk through the mapping — I've tentatively scheduled 2026-01-13 10:00 PT.

Subject: Initial CAIQ crosswalk + evidence manifest (OmniTrade)

Hi Jessica / Jonah,

Following up from our call — attached is the initial CAIQ crosswalk scoped to your requested control areas plus an evidence manifest. Summary below:

- File: redwood_caiq_crosswalk_omnitrade_v1.xlsx (attached) — mapping sheet includes CSA question id, our control name, owner, and recommended artifact filename.
- Evidence manifest (evidence_manifest_omnitrade.txt) — short descriptions and retention windows.
- Sample artifacts attached/linked: 
   * kvstore_kms_key_rotation_logs_2025-12.pdf (redacted log extract showing rotation events; note: HSM-backed rotations are indicated by an "HSM" column).
   * infra_arch_diagram_redwood_v2.png (VPC boundaries and peering lanes).
   * 30-day_log_extract_redacted.log (available in Drive link below — auditing logs are redacted for sensitive fields).

Key answers to your earlier question about rotation retention: we retain KMS rotation audit logs for 18 months by default; HSM-backed key material rotation events are recorded in the same rotation log with an HSM flag. The crosswalk highlights where this evidence satisfies CSA questions around key management (KMG-01/KMG-02 entries in the spreadsheet).

Open items we flagged in the spreadsheet: 
- A small number of controls related to partner-managed backups (marked "partner_scope") — we'll help facilitate contact with the partner if OmniTrade wants vendor evidence.
- Long-term archival retrieval SLA for logs older than 30 days (we provide 18-month retention but retrieval can take up to 48 hours for large exports).

Drive link with full bundle: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRedwoodOmniEvidence

Please review the crosswalk and call out any controls you'd like deeper evidence for; we can add screenshots or configuration exports on request.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Infrastructure Security 
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
